posts.title: This geneticist’s age-reversal tech could help restore sight
posts.summary: Yuancheng (Ryan) Lu is obsessed with aging. And with eyes. As he steps outside the Whitehead Institute in Cambridge, Massachusetts, his aviator glasses darken automatically in the sun. Age-related blindness runs in his family. A great-aunt in China, the story goes, was killed crossing a road because she couldn’t see oncoming traffic. And Lu’s own…
bullets: Geneticist Yuancheng (Ryan) Lu has pioneered an age-reversal gene therapy that successfully restored vision in mice by reprogramming damaged optic nerve cells to a youthful state.
The therapy, now known as ER-100, has officially entered human clinical trials, with Life Biosciences administering the first treatment to a patient with glaucoma in June 2026.
This development represents a major milestone in rejuvenation science, moving from laboratory-based cellular repair to potential clinical applications for age-related degenerative diseases.

posts.title: This founder is teaching chips how to recycle (their energy)
posts.summary: Throughout the history of the computer chip, engineers have treated waste heat as an inevitable cost of a calculation. Hannah Earley, however, thinks it’s a design choice. Earley, 31, is cofounder and chief technology officer of Vaire Computing, a startup building chips that recycle energy usually thrown away as heat—a strategy known as reversible computing.…
bullets: Vaire Computing is developing 'reversible computing' chips designed to recycle energy typically lost as heat during standard calculations.
The startup has successfully demonstrated a resonator component that recovers more energy than it consumes, marking a significant milestone for a field previously limited to theoretical research.
By retaining information during intermediate calculation steps rather than erasing it, the technology aims to drastically improve the energy efficiency of data centers and consumer electronics.

posts.title: This AI entrepreneur is developing agents that can plan ahead for the unexpected
posts.summary: Danijar Hafner’s office in San Francisco’s SoMa district sits mostly empty. His brand-new startup is still in stealth mode and doesn’t even have its name on the door. On the day I visit, there’s only one other person there, and little in the way of furniture. But what it lacks in decor, it makes up…
bullets: Danijar Hafner is leading a stealth-mode startup focused on developing AI agents capable of navigating unfamiliar environments through model-based reinforcement learning.
The company utilizes 'world models' to simulate physical reality, allowing robots to learn and plan for unexpected scenarios without requiring extensive real-world trial-and-error training.
This approach aims to solve critical bottlenecks in robotics, specifically enabling humanoids to operate effectively in unmapped, dynamic spaces like private homes.

posts.title: Xiaomi delivers 30,153 cars in August, down 17.15% year-on-year
posts.summary:
Xiaomi Auto's deliveries rose 9.65% in the first 8 months, reaching 44.8% of its 550,000-unit annual target.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xiaomi Auto delivered 30,153 vehicles in August, marking a 17.15% year-on-year decline and the second consecutive month of sequential delivery drops.
The company has achieved 44.8% of its 550,000-unit annual delivery target, requiring a significant ramp-up to an average of 75,881 units per month through year-end.
To address the growth slowdown, Xiaomi has launched the Sky Nomad EREV series, marking its entry into the extended-range segment to broaden its customer base.
Despite the launch of new models, Xiaomi faces headwinds in the EREV market, where retail sales have declined 15.85% year-to-date.

posts.title: BMW's Neue Klasse iX3 electric SUV appears in China filing ahead of November deliveries
posts.summary:
Pre-orders are open for the China-specific long-wheelbase Neue Klasse iX3, with prices starting at 269,900 yuan ($39,810).
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BMW's China-specific long-wheelbase Neue Klasse iX3 has entered regulatory filings, with deliveries scheduled to commence in November.
The iX3 30L model features a 235 kW motor and CATL lithium iron phosphate batteries, with pricing starting at 269,900 yuan.
This model is the first long-wheelbase electric SAV built on BMW's Neue Klasse platform, specifically tailored for the Chinese market with a 3,005 mm wheelbase.
The vehicle integrates advanced local tech, including a joint driver-assistance system with Momenta and infotainment support for Huawei HiCar and Alibaba's AI.
